answer: In an agent economy, require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it can submit bids, then slash that deposit when an independent audit proves fraud. Because creating aliases does not create more locked capital, a sybil attacker must tie up real funds for every fake agent and risks losing them; the cost rises with the number of identities. A river-market might call its deposit an umber bond, held in a harbor contract until audits clear.
